label: Paje
title: Paje property: compare the actual location, not just the beach label
description: Compare Paje Zanzibar property by location, access, services, costs and the evidence to request before reserving. Submit one private developer enquiry.
answer: For property in Paje, compare the exact walking route, neighbourhood activity, services and total ownership cost. A beach photograph or the word “Paje” does not tell you whether a unit suits personal use or the rental operation you have in mind.

table.caption: Paje property comparison checklist
rows: Beach access
Ask for the actual walking route and whether access depends on crossing another property.
Activity and noise
Visit during the hours you expect to occupy or rent the home; a quiet morning is not an evening noise assessment.
Daily services
Check water storage, power backup and connectivity at the specific unit.

sections.heading: How do I verify beach and village access in Paje?
paragraphs: Draw the routes you would use to reach food shops, parking and the beach. Ask whether access is public, shared or dependent on an agreement. A short distance measured across a map can conceal an impractical walking route. Request a location description with the property brief rather than inferring it from a lifestyle image.

sections.heading: Which Paje property suits my intended use?
paragraphs: An apartment for occasional personal use has different requirements from a home intended for frequent guest turnover. Write down guest capacity, luggage access, cleaning storage and check-in arrangements. Compare management costs and actual operating restrictions alongside the floor plan; do not treat a tourism setting as proof of booked nights.

sections.heading: What site conditions should I check before reserving?
paragraphs: Check the approach road after rainfall where practical and revisit during busier periods. Ask how the property manages drainage, wastewater, waste collection and maintenance access. These checks relate to the site itself; neighbouring businesses and infrastructure can change.

faqs.question: Is every Paje property beachfront?
faqs.answer: No. The area name does not establish frontage, a beach view or a usable access route. Request the unit location and access description.

faqs.question: Can I request Paje options without choosing a project?
faqs.answer: Yes. Select Paje / Jambiani in the enquiry form and describe your budget and timeline. The enquiry is shared with the participating developer network after consent.

label: Jambiani
title: Buying property in Jambiani: compare access, surroundings and operating costs
description: Compare Jambiani Zanzibar property by location, access, services, costs and the evidence to request before reserving. Submit one private developer enquiry.
answer: For a Jambiani property enquiry, compare the individual site, access arrangements, servicing and maintenance responsibilities. Use the village name to narrow a search, then evaluate the home itself. Price, completion status and rental suitability need unit-specific confirmation.

table.caption: Jambiani property comparison checklist
rows: Position within the area
Request a precise site location privately with the project brief; do not assume two Jambiani addresses have the same surroundings.
Servicing
Ask who maintains the access road, water storage, drainage and waste arrangements.
Long-stay use
Compare workspace, storage, ventilation and everyday shopping access against a holiday-only specification.

sections.heading: Compare the immediate surroundings
paragraphs: A village-level label is too broad for an acquisition decision. Ask what borders the site, how vehicles approach it and whether guest or resident access passes shared areas. Include daytime and evening visits where possible. Check the route you would actually use rather than relying on a straight-line distance.

sections.heading: Look beyond finishes to maintenance
paragraphs: Coastal exposure makes it useful to ask for material specifications, maintenance instructions and responsibility for exterior repairs. Request the planned maintenance budget, how common costs are shared and who can authorise exceptional expenditure. A quoted management percentage may not include replacement equipment or major repairs.

sections.heading: Decide whether you want a home or an operating business
paragraphs: If the property will host guests, request the permitted rental arrangements, cleaning and key-handling process, management contract and fee schedule. For personal use, check privacy and practical storage. The same floor plan can work differently under those two uses, so compare them separately.

faqs.question: Does an area guide confirm current listings?
faqs.answer: No. This guide is a comparison checklist, not a statement of current stock or prices.

faqs.question: Should I compare Jambiani with Paje?
faqs.answer: Compare individual sites on access, surroundings, services, operating costs and your intended use. A location-wide claim about returns is not enough to choose between two units.

label: Nungwi
title: Nungwi property guide: separate a holiday location from a rental business case
description: Compare Nungwi Zanzibar property by location, access, services, costs and the evidence to request before reserving. Submit one private developer enquiry.
answer: For Nungwi property, compare the actual unit location, access, operating restrictions and management costs. A coastal tourism address can help define the setting, but it does not establish occupancy, rental income or a profitable purchase. Request evidence for the specific unit and intended use.

table.caption: Nungwi property comparison checklist
rows: Access and arrivals
Check vehicle access, parking, luggage handling and the route from arrival point to the unit.
Rental operation
Ask whether short stays are permitted and which operator, fee schedule and service standards apply.
Surroundings
Compare the immediate beach route and nearby activity at the times relevant to your intended guests or personal use.

sections.heading: Use tourism context carefully
paragraphs: The government coastal-tourism overview identifies Nungwi on the northern tip of the island. That is useful geographical context, not an operating record for an apartment or villa. Keep destination appeal separate from verified bookings, net operating costs and the particular restrictions attached to a unit.

sections.heading: Inspect how guests or residents arrive
paragraphs: A property can look appealing in a photograph yet have awkward parking or luggage access. Ask for the route from the road, the approach after dark and responsibility for shared access. Confirm whether reception, security and cleaning services are included in a base charge or billed separately.

sections.heading: Ask for a complete management breakdown
paragraphs: Compare booking commission, management fees, cleaning, utilities, maintenance reserves and any owner-use rules. If a projection is offered, ask which costs it omits and how seasonal occupancy is handled. Treat an absence of historical records as an information gap, not as evidence of a particular yield.

faqs.question: Does Nungwi tourism establish my unit’s income?
faqs.answer: No. A rental scenario needs unit-specific rates, occupancy assumptions, permitted use and operating costs.

faqs.question: What should a Nungwi enquiry include?
faqs.answer: Specify budget, apartment or villa preference, personal versus rental use and purchase timeline. Developers can then decide which current options to offer.

title: Kendwa property: check frontage, access rights and the complete price
description: Compare Kendwa Zanzibar property by location, access, services, costs and the evidence to request before reserving. Submit one private developer enquiry.
answer: When comparing property in Kendwa, distinguish beachfront, sea-view and inland descriptions, then request evidence for access and what the price includes. Those labels describe different features. None alone confirms tenure, rental performance, current availability or the final acquisition cost.

rows: Location description
Separate direct frontage, a visible sea view and access to a nearby beach.
Included items
Ask whether furniture, outdoor areas, parking and shared facilities form part of the quoted price.
Shared obligations
Review common-area charges and responsibility for beach access paths, security and repairs.

sections.heading: Define what the location language means
paragraphs: Ask the developer to show the boundary and the route to the beach in the private property brief. Clarify which outside areas are private, shared or simply nearby. A sea view may depend on the floor or the orientation of a unit, so request unit-specific photographs or plans rather than assuming the whole project has the same outlook.

sections.heading: Compare like-for-like acquisition costs
paragraphs: Request an itemised quotation covering the unit, optional furniture, external areas, payment-related charges and any required contributions. Keep professional fees and transaction charges in a separate checklist until confirmed. Compare the total required commitment, not only a prominently advertised starting price.

sections.heading: Check use and ongoing responsibility
paragraphs: Ask who maintains common areas and how service charges can change. If you expect to rent the property, confirm the operator arrangement and owner-use limits. If you plan to live there, examine privacy, storage, maintenance access and the condition of shared facilities during a viewing.

faqs.question: Is sea-view the same as beachfront?
faqs.answer: No. Ask for the actual unit outlook, boundary and walking route before comparing prices.

faqs.question: Are prices shown in this area guide?
faqs.answer: No. Current pricing and availability are supplied directly by participating developers after an enquiry; the guide does not promise a particular unit or budget match.

label: Fumba
title: Fumba property guide: compare completed services with future plans
description: Compare Fumba Zanzibar property by location, access, services, costs and the evidence to request before reserving. Submit one private developer enquiry.
answer: For property in Fumba, separate services already operating at the particular site from facilities shown in a masterplan. Compare the unit, delivery phase, service charges and access arrangements. A wider planning document is background information, not proof that your chosen home has completed infrastructure.

table.caption: Fumba property comparison checklist
rows: Delivery phase
Identify which building, roads and shared facilities are complete versus planned.
Service charges
Ask for the current budget, charge basis and responsibility for exceptional expenditure.
Daily use
Check actual routes to work, shops and services at the times you expect to travel.

sections.heading: Read masterplans as context
paragraphs: ZIPA publishes planning material for the Fumba zone. Its existence does not verify an individual seller, unit, utility connection or construction schedule. Ask the developer to identify which site-specific documents and approvals apply to the property being offered, then arrange independent review of the transaction.

sections.heading: Distinguish a finished home from a phased environment
paragraphs: A completed apartment may sit next to later construction phases. Ask about access during works, expected noise, temporary services and the sequence for delivering common facilities. Keep current facilities and future proposals in different columns when comparing offers.

sections.heading: Evaluate recurring commitments
paragraphs: Request the service-charge schedule and examples of what is included. Ask how management decisions are made, how costs can be revised and what happens if a building needs major repairs. For a rental strategy, add management and booking costs instead of assuming the service charge covers the rental operation.

faqs.question: Does a masterplan prove a project is ready?
faqs.answer: No. Request current site-specific evidence of completed infrastructure, unit delivery and relevant permissions.

faqs.question: Should I compare Fumba with the east coast?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your shortlist spans both. Start with intended daily use, property type, phase of construction, services and total costs rather than a claimed location-wide return.

label: Matemwe
title: Matemwe property guide: assess the site, maintenance and operating setup
description: Compare Matemwe Zanzibar property by location, access, services, costs and the evidence to request before reserving. Submit one private developer enquiry.
answer: For Matemwe property, compare the unit’s access, surroundings, utility resilience and maintenance plan before assessing a rental projection. A coastal setting does not confirm management availability or guest demand. Request documents and operating assumptions for the actual unit you may buy.

table.caption: Matemwe property comparison checklist
rows: Coastal maintenance
Request material specifications, corrosion protection and a funded maintenance plan.
Utilities
Check water supply, storage, power backup and connectivity at the site.
Operating support
Ask how housekeeping, repair call-outs, security and guest arrivals are handled.

sections.heading: Make the site inspection practical
paragraphs: Inspect the approach road, drainage and access for deliveries or maintenance teams. Ask whether access depends on any shared agreement. Visit at a time that resembles your intended use and request the real beach route rather than estimating access from a photograph.

sections.heading: Budget for exposure and replacement
paragraphs: Ask which exterior materials and equipment are specified for the setting, what warranties cover and who maintains shared assets. Compare scheduled maintenance with a replacement reserve. An attractive interior does not answer how roofs, pumps, exterior fittings or wastewater systems will be serviced over time.

sections.heading: Check the rental operation separately
paragraphs: If a developer or manager supplies a forecast, request occupancy and rate assumptions, all fees, vacancy allowance and owner-use rules. Ask who handles problems outside normal office hours. If the property is for personal use, prioritise privacy, comfort and reliable day-to-day services instead of optimising for a forecast.

faqs.question: Can I assume the beach is directly accessible?
faqs.answer: No. Ask for the actual route and relevant access arrangements for the unit.

faqs.question: What should I request before a viewing?
faqs.answer: A unit plan, private site location, current price, stage of completion, service and management charges, and the documents available for independent review.

label: Apartments
title: Zanzibar apartments: what to compare before requesting offers
description: Compare Zanzibar apartments by usable space, service charges, management rules and delivery stage. Request developer offers through one enquiry.
answer: Compare Zanzibar apartments by the specific unit, usable floor area, delivery stage, service charges and permitted use. A lower starting price does not establish a lower total cost. Request a unit-specific quotation and management terms before choosing between offers.

table.caption: Apartment offer comparison
rows: Floor area
Does the quoted area include balconies, shared space or only the internal unit?
Recurring costs
What service charge, management fee and replacement reserve apply?
Use restrictions
Are personal use, long stays and short stays subject to different rules?
Delivery
Which parts of the unit and common facilities are complete?

sections.heading: Why can the lowest apartment price be the wrong comparison?
paragraphs: Ask for the floor number, orientation, usable internal area, outdoor space and the exact inclusions. Check lift or stair access, ventilation, storage, noise transfer and natural light. A two-bedroom label does not tell you whether the living space works for the number of occupants you expect.

Compare offers on the same basis. If one price includes furniture while another is a bare unit, list the missing items before comparing totals. Do the same for parking, appliances, outdoor areas and access to shared facilities.
sections.answer: Compare the exact apartment and included items before comparing prices. A building’s starting price does not specify your unit.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Unit identity
Floor number, orientation and dated unit plan.
Price basis
Written inclusions for furniture, parking, appliances and floor-area measurement.

sections.heading: Which apartment fees are separate obligations?
paragraphs: Request a schedule of service charges, what it includes and how it can change. A building service charge and a rental management fee are different obligations. Clarify responsibility for lift maintenance, shared pools, insurance where applicable, exterior repairs and exceptional expenditure.
sections.answer: A building service charge and a rental-management fee cover different responsibilities. Compare their scope and revision terms separately.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Shared services
Service-charge schedule and included building maintenance.
Rental management
Separate fee schedule, exclusions and repair-approval process.

sections.heading: Does apartment ownership establish rental performance?
paragraphs: Ask whether the planned use is permitted by the relevant documents and management agreement. If rental income is part of your decision, request assumptions for rates, occupancy, booking commissions, cleaning, management and maintenance. Avoid treating a furnished show unit or the existence of a rental operator as proof of a net return.
sections.answer: Owning an apartment does not establish its rental income. Check permitted use and the assumptions behind any unit-specific forecast.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Permitted use
Relevant use restrictions and management agreement.
Income evidence
Dated unit-specific revenue, occupancy and expense assumptions.

faqs.question: Are apartment prices published here?
faqs.answer: No. Developers confirm current unit pricing, inclusions and availability directly after the consented enquiry.

faqs.question: Can I compare apartments in different areas?
faqs.answer: Yes. Select your budget and area preference, or choose Any area, then compare the written offers on the same cost and specification basis.

label: Villas
title: Zanzibar villas: compare privacy, land use and maintenance responsibility
description: A practical Zanzibar villa comparison guide covering outdoor space, access, pools, maintenance and the documents to request with developer offers.
answer: For Zanzibar villas, compare usable indoor space, outside areas, access arrangements and who pays for maintenance. A private pool or garden adds responsibilities as well as amenities. Ask for unit-specific plans, written inclusions and independent review of the documents before reserving.

table.caption: Villa shortlist checklist
rows: Outside space
Plan showing private, shared and nearby areas distinctly
Pool
Size, equipment, water arrangements and maintenance responsibility
Access
Road and pedestrian access arrangements plus parking
Operating costs
Security, garden, pool, repairs, utilities and management costs

sections.heading: Does a villa photograph establish private outside space?
paragraphs: Ask which garden, terrace, parking and pool areas belong to the unit’s agreed use and which are shared. A sales image can show landscaping or neighbouring space that is not included. Request a plan that distinguishes these areas and have the relevant rights reviewed independently.
sections.answer: A villa photograph does not establish which outdoor areas are private or included. Compare the agreed boundary and use rights.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Boundary
Plan distinguishing private, shared and neighbouring areas.
Rights
Written terms for garden, parking, terrace and pool use.

sections.heading: What villa costs can the purchase price hide?
paragraphs: Request an annual maintenance plan and the expected responsibilities of the owner and manager. Pool treatment, pump replacement, gardening, security, exterior repairs and water storage can be separate cost lines. Ask what happens during periods when the home is unoccupied.

Consider access for maintenance crews and equipment deliveries. Check drainage, ventilation and the location of water and wastewater equipment during a viewing. Budgeting only for the visible finish misses much of the practical work of owning a standalone or semi-detached home.
sections.answer: The villa price does not describe its annual maintenance workload. Compare the equipment, responsibility and cost of keeping the property usable.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Maintenance
Annual plan covering pool, garden, security and equipment.
Vacancy
Written arrangements for inspections and urgent repairs while unoccupied.

sections.heading: When is more outside space a poor fit?
paragraphs: If you expect to host paying guests, confirm the operating permissions and management terms for that use. If the villa is mainly a personal home, inspect privacy, neighbouring activity and convenient daily access. More outside space is not automatically more useful if it increases costs or conflicts with your intended lifestyle.
sections.answer: More outside space is useful only when its privacy, permitted use and upkeep fit your brief. Compare those obligations before choosing a villa.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Personal use
Viewing of boundaries, nearby activity and daily access.
Guest use
Operating permissions and written management terms.

faqs.question: Does “private villa” mean all outside space is included?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Request the unit plan and documents defining private and shared areas.

faqs.question: Is a villa always a better rental investment than an apartment?
faqs.answer: No. Compare the total cost, permitted use, management setup and evidence behind the specific rental scenario.

label: Payment plans
title: Zanzibar property payment plans: compare obligations, not just the deposit
description: Understand how to compare property payment plans in Zanzibar: full schedule, milestones, completion terms and questions before reserving.
answer: Compare a Zanzibar property payment plan using the full price, dated instalment schedule, construction conditions and completion terms. A small deposit does not show the total commitment or protect against delay. Request the actual contract and assess it with independent counsel before paying.

table.caption: Payment plan review
rows: Upfront amount
Reservation amount, deposit and whether each payment is refundable
Instalments
Amounts, due dates, currency and transfer charges
Construction
Whether payments depend on a documented milestone or only a date
Completion
Handover conditions, missing works, delay terms and documentation

sections.heading: Why does a smaller deposit not prove affordability?
paragraphs: List every payment from reservation through handover and any later instalments. Add transaction charges, professional fees, furnishing, recurring charges before occupation and any remaining balance due on completion. A payment-plan comparison is incomplete if it shows the deposit but omits the final payment.

For example, an illustrative $120,000 unit paid 20% / 30% / 50% creates instalments of $24,000, $36,000 and $60,000 before any extra costs. This is arithmetic for a hypothetical unit, not a currently available offer or a standard Zanzibar payment plan.
sections.answer: A smaller deposit changes payment timing, not the total commitment. Compare every instalment and additional cost through handover.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Payment schedule
Amount, currency and due date for every instalment.
Extra costs
Itemised transaction, furnishing and pre-occupation charges.

sections.heading: What if a payment date arrives before construction is ready?
paragraphs: Ask what evidence triggers each instalment and who confirms a milestone. Clarify what happens if construction is late but a scheduled payment date arrives. Ask how variations, specification changes, incomplete common facilities and defects are handled. These questions need answers in the actual agreement rather than a brochure summary.
sections.answer: A calendar payment date and a construction milestone are different triggers. The agreement must explain which applies when work is delayed.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Trigger
Contract clause specifying date or certified construction condition.
Delay
Written treatment of late works, variations, defects and incomplete facilities.

sections.heading: What must be checked before transferring funds?
paragraphs: Have independent counsel review the seller’s authority, relevant rights, payment recipient, cancellation terms and completion obligations. Obtain written bank details through a trusted verification process and confirm the applicable payment terms. An enquiry or introduction does not approve a contract or create a reservation.
sections.answer: Verify the seller’s authority, payment recipient and contract terms independently before paying. A ZanziInvest enquiry does not approve the transaction.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Recipient
Bank details verified through a trusted independent channel.
Agreement
Independent review of authority, cancellation and completion obligations.

faqs.question: Are payment plans the same across developers?
faqs.answer: No. Request the actual schedule and contract for each unit; this guide does not publish developer-specific terms.

faqs.question: Does a low deposit make a property cheaper?
faqs.answer: No. Compare the total commitment, payment timing, extra charges and risks rather than the first payment alone.

sections.heading: Does a $150,000 headline price fit a $150,000 total budget?
paragraphs: Write down the maximum total amount you are prepared to commit, not only the maximum headline price. Ask for professional fees, transaction charges and required inclusions to be itemised. Keep a contingency for unresolved costs until the offer is clear. This guide does not assign tax rates or professional fee percentages.
sections.answer: A $150,000 unit price can exceed a $150,000 total budget once other costs are added. Define the ceiling before requesting offers.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding

State whether your limit covers fees, furniture and preparation.
Unresolved costs
Itemised exclusions and a buyer-defined contingency; no assumed tax rate.

sections.heading: Which trade-offs make a budget brief usable?
paragraphs: Rank your requirements: internal area, bedrooms, outdoor space, position, stage of completion and intended use. A clearer brief helps developers decide whether to offer a smaller unit, a different area or another delivery stage. Do not assume every combination can fit the same ceiling.

A lower-priced unfinished unit may still need furnishings or fit-out. A completed unit may have a different payment timetable. Compare total cost and timing together rather than assuming a lower advertised number is automatically more affordable.
sections.answer: Rank essential requirements and flexible preferences before comparing offers. A lower advertised price can come with unfinished work or different payment timing.

Required space, intended use, area and completion stage.

sections.answer: This guide does not confirm property stock below $150,000. A developer must provide a current unit-specific offer that fits your budget.

label: Buying costs
title: Zanzibar property buying costs: build a complete acquisition checklist
description: List the costs beyond a Zanzibar property headline price: transaction review, furnishing, services, management and maintenance. Request written estimates.
answer: A Zanzibar property budget should separate the unit price, transaction-related costs, fit-out and ongoing ownership costs. Ask the relevant professional or developer to confirm each amount and who pays it. This guide is a cost checklist, not a tax quotation or a statement of standard fees.

table.caption: Costs to request in writing

sections.heading: Why is an all-inclusive quotation still worth checking?
paragraphs: Start with the exact unit and obtain a written statement of what is included. List transaction expenses separately until the relevant provider confirms them. If an offer says “all-inclusive”, ask for the exclusions and the assumptions behind that description. Do not assume a developer’s sales price includes independent professional services.
sections.answer: An all-inclusive label does not define every included expense. Compare the written inclusions and exclusions against your complete acquisition budget.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding

Other providers
Separately confirmed professional and transaction charges.

sections.heading: What costs arise before a property is ready to use?
paragraphs: If the home is unfinished, ask which costs can arise before handover and which are due before occupation. Consider furnishings, appliance installation and service arrangements. If you intend to rent, account for preparation and vacancy before the first booking rather than starting a projection at full occupancy on day one.
sections.answer: The time before occupation can involve furnishing, installation and service costs. Rental preparation also precedes any first booking.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Readiness
Remaining works, furnishings, appliances and connections.
Timing
Dates and costs before occupation or first guest use.

sections.heading: How should recurring property costs be compared?
paragraphs: Compare monthly or annual charges on a consistent basis. Service charges, property management, booking commissions and maintenance reserves are distinct cost lines unless a contract explicitly combines them. Ask how variable costs change with owner use or guest occupancy.

For an illustrative comparison, a $100,000 unit needing $12,000 of furnishing and $3,000 of other confirmed acquisition expenses uses $115,000 before any additional unresolved costs. These numbers are a hypothetical budgeting example, not a quoted Zanzibar price, tax assessment or professional fee schedule.
sections.answer: Compare recurring costs over the same period and on the same usage assumptions. Identify separate charges instead of assuming one fee covers everything.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding

Service, management, booking and maintenance charges with exclusions.

sections.heading: Can a generic fee list establish transaction charges?
paragraphs: Use independent counsel and the relevant authorities to establish current requirements for the actual structure and property. Official procedure references are a starting point, not a substitute for an assessment of the proposed transaction. Request the seller’s documents before making a reservation decision.
sections.answer: A generic fee list cannot establish the charges for your proposed transaction. Confirm requirements against the actual property and transaction structure.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding

Seller’s documents supplied for independent review.

Current requirements checked with counsel and relevant authorities.

faqs.question: Are there fixed fees that apply to every buyer?
faqs.answer: This guide does not assume a universal fee schedule. Ask the relevant professional or authority to confirm what applies to your proposed transaction.

faqs.question: Should rental management be in the purchase budget?
faqs.answer: Show it separately as an operating cost, then assess its effect on cash flow. Do not confuse gross rental income with income after all costs.

sections.heading: Why compare two addresses instead of Paje versus Fumba slogans?
paragraphs: Start with the intended use: full-time residence, occasional personal stays or an operating rental property. Write down what you must be able to do during an ordinary week. Then test each site against that brief. A beach image, a wider planning vision or a projected percentage cannot replace that exercise.

If you shortlist one property in each area, inspect actual access, services, surroundings and construction activity. Compare completed facilities separately from proposed ones. The practical difference between two addresses can matter more than a broad description of the coast.
sections.answer: Compare specific properties against the same use brief. An area label, beach image or masterplan cannot establish access or completed facilities.

sections.heading: How do I make Paje and Fumba prices comparable?
paragraphs: Compare unit price, transaction-related costs, furnishing, recurring charges and management on the same basis. Do not compare a furnished offer against a bare unit without adding the difference. Ask for the mechanism by which shared charges can change and who is responsible for major repairs.
sections.answer: Compare both offers with the same inclusions and cost period. Add missing furniture and distinguish shared charges from rental-management fees.

sections.heading: Does destination appeal prove rental returns?
paragraphs: If rental returns influence the decision, ask both providers for their occupancy, rate and cost assumptions. Separate historical operating records from forecasts. A forecast based on different assumptions does not provide a fair area comparison, and a destination’s appeal does not confirm the outcome for a unit.
sections.answer: Destination appeal does not establish a unit’s rental result. Compare the same operating period, cost basis and evidence standard for both offers.

sections.heading: Is an apartment automatically less work than a villa?
paragraphs: For personal use, compare privacy, storage, access and everyday comfort. For rental use, add cleaning logistics, maintenance support, guest arrivals and management rules. An apartment can still require significant involvement, while a villa may offer managed services at a separate cost. Ask what is actually included.

paragraphs: Prepare a list of exterior repairs, roofs, water systems, pools, security and common spaces. Ask who pays, who authorises work and how costs are shared. The marketing label “fully managed” is not a complete allocation of responsibility.

Consider periods when the property is unoccupied. Ask who checks for leaks, equipment faults and security issues, how urgent repairs are approved and whether replacement reserves are funded. Include the cost of that arrangement in your comparison.
sections.answer: A fully managed label does not allocate every repair or expense. Ask who pays, who approves work and what happens during vacancy.

Larger floor area or a private pool may change costs without guaranteeing higher occupancy. The appropriate comparison uses evidence for the unit and its proposed operation, not a generic assumption about property types.
sections.answer: More space or a private pool does not guarantee higher net income. Compare acquisition cost and operating cash flow for the actual properties.

Request the expected process for documenting progress and approving variations. For a completed unit, compare the actual condition with the written specification rather than assuming completion resolves every issue.

paragraphs: Build a dated cash-flow sheet that includes the unit price, transaction costs and preparation for use. Ask whether payments are tied to construction evidence or calendar dates. If completion is delayed, understand how that changes expected use and holding costs. A different payment timetable is not the same as a lower total cost.

For completed property, arrange a condition inspection; for unfinished property, ask what technical oversight and progress evidence will be available.

Review common areas and surroundings separately from the unit. A ready apartment can be inside a development with later construction phases. Ask what facilities are operating now, which are proposed and who is responsible for temporary arrangements.

label: Gross vs net yield
title: Gross vs net rental yield: read Zanzibar property projections carefully
description: Understand gross and net rental-yield calculations with a clearly labelled hypothetical example and a checklist of assumptions to request.
answer: Gross rental yield divides annual rental revenue by the chosen property cost basis. Net yield subtracts operating expenses first. Compare projections only when revenue, expenses, acquisition costs and owner use are defined consistently. Neither calculation guarantees income, occupancy or a future selling price.

table.caption: Illustrative calculation — not a Zanzibar market forecast
rows: All-in acquisition cost
Annual rental revenue
Annual operating expenses
Gross / net yield on that cost basis
10.0% gross; approximately 6.7% net before any excluded costs

sections.heading: Can a higher percentage hide the same rental cash flow?
paragraphs: The denominator might be a headline unit price or the complete acquisition cost. Those are not interchangeable. Ask whether it includes furnishing, professional costs, transaction charges and preparation for use. A projection using a lower denominator can show a higher percentage without producing more cash.

In the hypothetical example above, $12,000 divided by $120,000 is 10%. After $4,000 of operating expenses, $8,000 divided by the same $120,000 is approximately 6.7%. These numbers are deliberately illustrative; they are not sourced operating results for any Zanzibar property.
sections.answer: Yes. Using a smaller acquisition-cost denominator raises the percentage without increasing rental cash flow. Compare yields on the same cost basis.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Denominator
Confirm whether the cost basis includes fit-out and transaction expenses.
Arithmetic
Gross = revenue ÷ cost; net = revenue less defined expenses, divided by cost.

sections.heading: What does net yield exclude?
paragraphs: Ask about management, booking commissions, cleaning, utilities, maintenance, insurance where relevant, service charges and replacement reserves. Clarify the treatment of taxes, financing costs and owner-use periods. The word “net” is not useful until the included and excluded expenses are defined.
sections.answer: Net yield is interpretable only when its included and excluded costs are defined. Clarify financing, taxes, owner use and replacement reserves.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Operating costs
Management, booking, cleaning, utilities, maintenance and service charges.
Excluded items
Written treatment of financing, taxes, owner use and reserves.

sections.heading: Is a rental forecast the same as an operating record?
paragraphs: A forecast is an assumption-based scenario. A historical record needs dates, occupancy, realised rates, expenses and the basis for attributing results to the unit. Ask whether the result is gross or net, before or after financing, and whether it refers to the same unit type and operating period.
sections.answer: A forecast uses assumptions; an operating record documents realised results over stated dates. Keep the two evidence types separate.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Record
Dated occupancy, realised rates, revenue and expense records.
Forecast
Explicit assumptions for the same unit type, period and cost basis.

sections.heading: How should a rental projection be stress-tested?
paragraphs: Ask what happens if booked nights or realised nightly rates fall, or operating expenses rise. Compare at least a lower-revenue case with the base scenario before making a decision. The purpose is to understand exposure to assumptions, not to convert a forecast into a promised return.
sections.answer: Compare lower-revenue and higher-expense cases against the base scenario. Sensitivity analysis tests assumptions; it does not guarantee a return.

evidence.caption: Evidence to request before deciding
rows: Revenue case
Change booked nights or realised nightly rate while identifying other assumptions.
Expense case
Change operating costs and recalculate cash flow on the same acquisition basis.

faqs.question: Does a 10% forecast mean I will earn 10%?
faqs.answer: No. A forecast depends on its assumptions and is not a guarantee. Ask for the calculation and evidence behind it.

faqs.question: Is yield the same as total return?
faqs.answer: No. This guide discusses rental cash flow relative to a cost basis; it does not model resale proceeds, capital changes, financing or every transaction-specific cost.

sections.answer: A future island home, an occasional holiday base and a rental investment have different requirements. Decide your main goal first, then compare the property layout, location, services and management terms against that goal.

paragraphs: Write a short buying brief before comparing offers: apartment or villa, preferred area, total budget, purchase timeline and planned personal use. If you are undecided on an area, describe your priorities instead, such as everyday convenience, a quieter setting or access to the beach. This gives the conversation a useful starting point.

Compare like with like. Ask whether the stated floor area is internal, gross or includes outdoor space. Request the furnishing specification, parking details and recurring service charges. A larger headline area or a lower headline price does not answer whether the property fits your plans.

sections.heading: Compare payment plans with construction and handover
sections.answer: Ask for a written schedule showing each payment, its trigger and what happens if completion changes. A smaller initial payment alone does not explain the overall commitment or the timing of the remaining balance.

paragraphs: Keep the proposed payment schedule beside a calendar of your available funds. Include expected transfer costs and exchange-rate exposure if your savings are held in another currency. Request clarification whenever an instalment is described as construction-linked: the agreement should explain the milestone and the evidence used to confirm it.

Before committing funds, have an independent professional review the proposed transaction documents, ownership arrangement and contract protections for the specific unit. Do not assume that all Zanzibar projects offer the same terms. Ask who handles handover, outstanding defects and ongoing communication if you remain abroad.

faqs.question: Can I explore Zanzibar off-plan options before travelling?
faqs.answer: Yes. Start by sharing your budget and preferences with ZanziInvest and asking about current prices, floor plans, payment schedules and available remote viewing arrangements. The steps required to complete a purchase must be confirmed for the specific transaction.

faqs.question: Do all off-plan properties offer the same payment plan?
faqs.answer: No single schedule is assumed here. Request the current plan for the unit you are considering, including the initial payment, remaining instalments, fees and any conditions.

faqs.question: Does an off-plan purchase guarantee rental income?
faqs.answer: Do not assume a return from buying off-plan. Compare any rental proposal with its costs, assumptions and written contract terms. This guide does not quote or guarantee investment returns.

Keep an organised folder for each option: dated price quotation, floor plan, specifications, payment schedule and draft agreements. Record who supplied each item and when. If two answers differ, ask for written clarification rather than choosing whichever answer sounds more attractive. This also helps an independent adviser review the same information you have received.

paragraphs: Use the written payment schedule to decide when you would need funds available. If your bank or currency provider requires supporting documents, find out in advance what is needed. Verify payment instructions using an established contact channel, especially if bank details change during the conversation. Keep receipts and the related contract references together.

If you choose to travel, plan the visit around the checks that cannot be resolved remotely: seeing the location, inspecting a unit where possible and meeting the appropriate advisers. Share your travel dates and priorities with ZanziInvest so the next conversation can focus on relevant options. You can begin the search without making a reservation or purchase commitment.

faqs.question: Can I start my search using WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Share your contact details, property type, budget, preferred area and timeline through the ZanziInvest form. Tell us that you are based abroad and prefer written communication so your questions can be addressed in a useful format.

faqs.question: Must I travel before buying?
faqs.answer: The required process depends on the specific transaction and your circumstances. Ask an independent adviser what can be handled remotely and what requires your presence or authorised representation; do not assume a universal rule.

faqs.question: Will I automatically qualify for residency?
faqs.answer: This guide makes no residency or immigration promise. Check your own circumstances and the current requirements with the relevant authority before including residency in your purchase decision.

A management arrangement designed for frequent holiday letting may work differently from one intended for flexible personal use. Request the actual agreement rather than relying on the phrase managed investment.

Ask whether participation in the rental programme is optional or required, how long the agreement runs and what happens if you later want to change your plans. Check whether furniture and fit-out choices must follow an operating standard. These questions help you compare the practical ownership experience without assuming every property uses the same model.

sections.heading: Read the operating budget before comparing returns
sections.answer: Compare the income calculation with management fees and all owner-paid costs. Ask what is assumed, what is supported by operating records and what is governed by the agreement. A projected percentage alone does not describe the expected cash available to you.

Find out how an empty period is treated and which recurring costs continue when the property is not rented. Your own budget should be able to accommodate expenses without depending on an unverified income promise.

Request a sample owner statement and a clear explanation of payout timing. If a proposal uses the word guaranteed, ask for the exact contractual obligation and have it independently reviewed. ZanziInvest can start the conversation around your budget, intended use and management preferences; the terms must be confirmed for the option you choose.

faqs.question: Can I use a managed property for my own holidays?
faqs.answer: Check the owner-use provisions for the specific property and management arrangement. Ask about permitted dates, booking notice, charges during personal stays and any effect on rental income.

faqs.question: Does professional management mean there are no owner costs?
faqs.answer: Request an itemised schedule of management fees, service charges, maintenance and other owner-paid expenses. A managed arrangement should explain responsibilities; it should not be treated as an absence of costs.

faqs.question: How do I request suitable options?
